method.description: Shifts the position of the specified bullet by the given offset.

method.name: wake_bullet
method.description: Alias for [method enable_bullet] with unambiguous naming: revives one pooled or manually-disabled slot with its current appearance/ballistics intact (same-owner re-enable). Cross-owner reuse must go through the factory spawn methods or enable_volley(), which reseed appearance, custom data, speeds and patterns.

members.member: Whether each bullet's direction is adjusted based on rotation data (the bullet moves where it faces). Mirrors the spawn data flag; pool reuse re-applies the data value.

Whether an oncoming target amplifies the rebound through relative reflection, set live. True (default) enables the extra kick; false reflects absolutely. Outcome guarantee: the committed reflection always separates along the contact normal. Target velocity is sampled when the overlap is queued (scripts changing it before the drain cannot corrupt the bounce), and any stale or degenerate relative frame falls back to the absolute reflection, so target motion can only add energy, never send the bullet through the target.

Quiet period in seconds after a bounce, set live (finite in [0, 1]). Swallows further bounce records whatever they hit, so keep it small and use [member bounce_debounce_sec] for repeat suppression. Example: bullet clips two walls 0.03 s apart with cooldown 0.05: the first touch bounces, the second is swallowed.

Same-target debounce window in seconds, set live (finite, 0 or more, no upper cap). Inside the window a re-hit against the just-bounced object never re-bounces; other targets bounce freely (unlike [member bounce_cooldown_sec], which swallows every target). 0 disables it. Example: bullet slides along one wall with debounce 0.15: it bounces once, ignores that wall for 0.15 s, but still bounces off a second wall touched in between.
Whether a bounce also counts as a normal hit, set live. False (default) means free bounces. A consumed bounce emits BOTH the bounce signal and the matching area/body signal.

Bitmask of target collision layers that trigger a bounce, set live. Takes precedence over the normal collision path. 0 (default) disables bouncing. Spawn-time equivalent lives on [member BulletVolleyData2D.bounce_mask] (reseeded on every pool reuse).
How many times a single bullet may bounce before bounces stop for it, set live. 0 (default) = unlimited. Read per-bullet progress with [method bullet_get_bounce_count].

Which surface normal to reflect across, set live: 0 Simple Radial, 1 Precise Shape (rectangle, circle, capsule, segment, world boundary; falls back to radial for convex polygons or without a usable target shape).

Whether a same-direction target feeds its velocity into the bounce, set live. True (default) surges pushed bullets forward instead of reversing them; false reflects absolutely. Same outcome guarantee as [member bounce_charge_amplify]: separation along the contact normal always holds.
Random scatter in degrees around the reflected heading per bounce, set live (finite in [0, 180]).
Whether a bounce re-aims the bullet visual at the reflected heading, set live.
Max visual turn rate in radians/sec toward the reflected heading, set live. 0 snaps instantly; above 0 only the sprite slews. Ignored while [member adjust_direction_based_on_rotation] is on.

Speed multiplier applied on every bounce, set live (finite, 0 or more, no upper cap). 1.0 is perfectly elastic, 0 dead-stops. The boost sticks: the bounce raises the bullet's cached max speed to the new speed and a per-bullet multiplier persists across speed-curve overwrites. Moving targets contribute their velocity when [member bounce_push_assist] (same-direction) or [member bounce_charge_amplify] (oncoming) is on; repeat hits against the same target while separating never re-bounce.
Live TileMapLayer opt-in: toggling rebuilds nothing, the next drain reads it. Same head-on reflection contract as the spawn-data flag.

Whether the current homing target should be automatically popped from the deque once it gets reached by a bullet (per-bullet deques only).
Adjust the distance for considering a target reached with [member homing_distance_before_reached].
The signal [signal bullet_homing_target_reached] is emitted when a target is reached.
If you want this behavior for the shared deque, use [member shared_homing_deque_auto_pop_after_target_reached] instead.
How many times a bullet can collide before it gets disabled. If you set to 0, then the bullet will NEVER get disabled due to collisions.

An array of integers representing the current collision count for each bullet. The index of each integer in the array corresponds to the bullet index it is meant to represent.
For example, if you have 3 bullets and their current collision counts are 1, 2 and 3 respectively, then this array would be [1, 2, 3].
You can use this property to keep track of how many times each bullet has collided, and you can also set it to update the collision counts as needed.

When on (default), a bullet reports each target object at most once per drain window, even when the physics server reports several shape pairs for one overlap (multi-shape bodies and areas). Off restores legacy shape-level delivery: every shape record counts, signals and bounces separately.
The elapsed time used for the bullets' curves. This is the time that gets passed to the curves assigned to the bullets, you can manipulate it freely.

Stackable sprite-effect layers (trails, spawn flashes, hit sparks, destroy explosions, bounce sparks, lifetime fizzles, manual-clear puffs). Each entry renders through its own per-frame shards: one extra draw call per animation frame while anything is visible, zero when idle. Empty (default) disables the whole feature. Assign custom SpriteFrames per layer. Cost scales with art (frames), bullets, and active one-shots, not with layer count alone.
Runtime twin of [member BulletVolleyData2D.emit_collision_signals] (reset from the spawn data on every new life).

Fade-in seconds after spawn (0 disables). The volley starts at transparent base tint and reaches full tint at fade_in_sec. Works with infinite lifetimes. While any fade is configured the tick owns self_modulate: retint through [method set_fade_base_modulate], not the CanvasItem setter.
Fade-out seconds before expiry (0 disables). Needs a finite lifetime: infinite volleys ignore it.

Shared gravity acceleration in px/s^2, filling only genuine per-bullet gaps (2D sideview arcs, tower-defense shells). (0, 0) disables — top-down default. Writing it starts a new regime only for the slots it changes: user-authored per-bullet entries (spawn-data vectors, even deliberate zeros, or [method bullet_set_gravity] writes) are kept with their fall speed intact, while gap slots take the shared value and restart theirs. A slot that took the shared value stays a gap, so the next write still reaches it. Prefer [method bullet_set_gravity] for single slots.
Seconds of straight flight before gravity starts integrating. 0 falls immediately.
Seconds of falling before gravity stops integrating (volley glides on with frozen fall speed). 0 = infinite.
Seconds of straight flight before steering starts (classic aimed-then-homing). 0 steers immediately.

Adjust if you want your bullets to consider a homing target reached if they are within a certain distance away from it.
The [signal bullet_homing_target_reached] signal is emitted when a target is reached.
Seconds of steering before bullets fly straight (lets fast players escape). 0 is infinite.
Steering pauses while the bullet is farther than this from its target. 0 is unlimited.

Adjust this value for natural smooth turning. Test with values [code]0.00-20.00[/code] or even bigger. Latch note: the first per-bullet write ([method bullet_set_homing_smoothing]) snapshots every sibling at the current shared value, so later shared writes only affect never-latched volleys — call [method clear_per_bullet_homing_smoothing] to hand control back to shared. The spawner equivalent fans [code]homing_smoothing_start + homing_smoothing_step * i[/code] per slot.

If you set to true then the texture of the bullets will start facing the direction in which it is moving while homing towards a target. Leave it off and homing targets will not steer bullets at all (unless a movement pattern or rotation data does), and you get one warning about it.
How often it should cache the position of the targets so that they can be re-used instead of fetching them every frame. Increase if you want to boost performance.

Velocity added to every bullet for its whole life, e.g. the emitter's momentum ([member BulletSpawner2D.inherit_movement_velocity]). Homing bullets aim through it: they cancel its part across the line of sight to the target, as long as their own speed is larger than that part.

Whether the attachments auto pooling is enabled or not.
When enabled, the attachments will automatically get pushed to the object pool when the bullets get disabled. When disabled, the attachments will automatically get freed from the scene tree upon collision.

Whether the volley returns to the factory's pool when its last bullet is disabled (default on). Pooling releases everything the volley held for its owner: attachments, homing targets, orbit state, timers, pending hits, its own signal connections and user resources; the handle is then stale ([method is_pooled]). With it off, the volley parks instead ([method is_parked]): frozen and still yours, so [method enable_bullet] can wake it later with all its state. Turning it on for a parked volley pools it right away. Note: both pooling flags are per-instance state, not spawn data; [method reset_pooling_flags_to_default] restores them.

If you set to true, then the lifetime will be ignored and bullets will never be destroyed.
Warning: If you don't implement "collision walls" or anything else to intercept/collide with the bullets, then they will truly live forever in your memory and you will experience lag.
Linear drag trimming speed each tick. 0 disables.
Live tint-over-life gradient, sampled by lifetime fraction and multiplied with the fade base and fades. Reseeded from spawn data on every spawn/enable. Null disables it.
Live bullet whiten override: toggling rebuilds the cached animation frames whitened (alpha preserved) or restores the art. Reseeded from spawn data on every spawn/enable.

A shared [BulletCurvesData2D] resource that can be assigned to all bullets in the volley. This is useful for saving memory if you have a lot of bullets that share the same curves data, since you can assign the same resource to all of them instead of creating a new one for each bullet. Values are copied at set time: editing the resource in place afterwards changes nothing until you set it again. Direction channels never park the direction at zero: an Override result near zero keeps the incoming direction.

Fallback spin for bullets whose own rotation entry is missing or invalid, set live. Only fully-zero triples (the invalid-entry gap marker) are filled; bullets with any non-zero value keep it. Live writes fill once at call time (order matters: per-zero then shared fills, shared then per-zero stays zero). All-zero shared is a silent no-op; non-finite shared aborts the whole fallback with an error. Clearing it (null) keeps the current ballistics. Configure the spawn-time equivalent (plus its [code]tile_*[/code] checkbox) on [BulletVolleyData2D]. Negative spin is legal and clamps symmetrically to [-max, max].

Fallback speed for bullets whose own speed entry is missing or invalid, set live. Only fully-zero triples (the invalid-entry gap marker) are filled; bullets with any non-zero value keep it. Live writes fill once at call time (order matters: per-zero then shared fills, shared then per-zero stays zero). All-zero shared is a silent no-op; non-finite shared aborts the whole fallback with an error. Clearing it (null) keeps the current ballistics. Configure the spawn-time equivalent (plus its [code]tile_*[/code] checkbox) on [BulletVolleyData2D]. Note: shared movement-speed curves still outrank it per tick. Negative speed flies backwards, clamped to [-max, max].

Fallback wobble for bullets without a live per-bullet wobble resource, set live. Setting it re-seeds only those slots; clearing it (null) deactivates exactly those slots. Spawn-time equivalent (plus its [code]tile_all_bullet_wobble_data[/code] checkbox) lives on [member BulletVolleyData2D.shared_bullet_wobble_data]. Example: [code]bullets.set_shared_bullet_wobble_data(wobble)[/code] adds sway to every plain bullet while custom per-bullet seeds keep theirs.
You can edit the custom bullets data that the volley was spawned with. Use this to set damage data or anything else you want to store in a resource for your bullets to use.

Whether the current homing target should be automatically popped from the deque once it gets reached by a bullet (shared deque only).
Adjust the distance for considering a target reached with [member homing_distance_before_reached].
The signal [signal bullet_homing_target_reached] is emitted when a target is reached.
If you want this behavior for the per-bullet deques, use [member bullet_homing_auto_pop_after_target_reached] instead.

signal.name: bullet_homing_target_reached
signal.description: Emitted live, inside the physics tick, when a bullet comes within [member homing_distance_before_reached] of its homing target. [param target] is null for position and mouse targets; [param target_global_position] is always valid. With auto pop on, the reached target is popped after the handler, unless the handler already changed the front of the deque (a target it pushed survives). Connections made directly on the volley are dropped when it returns to the pool: connect to [signal BulletSpawner2D.volley_bullet_homing_target_reached] for spawner volleys.

signal.name: sprite_animation_finished
signal.description: Emitted live, once, when a non-looping SpriteFrames animation reaches its last frame. Re-armed by every play or restart.
